Another indicator of low social economic status is education: over 70% of the caretakers had no formal education or only primary education (Table 1). Low education limits financial status and understanding of child care and nutrition, and poor social economic status may lead to comorbidities such as intestinal worms, causing recurrent blood loss and anemia, as reported by [@w:w13] in Ethiopia.

It is also important to note that undernutrition is often associated with micronutrient deficiencies [@w:w12], as affirmed by the predominantly microcytic anemia in this study (Table 3), mainly due to iron deficiency. Education is another indicator of low social economic status: over 70% of the caretakers never had a formal education or only a primary education (Table 1). Low education limits financial status and understanding of child care and nutrition, while poor social economic status may cause intestinal worm infestation, with recurrent blood loss and anemia, as reported by [@w:w13] in Ethiopia.
